newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Explosion kills 40, wounds 150 in Afghan city.
newsitem.headline: Explosion kills 40, wounds 150 in Afghan city.

text.p: About 40 people were killed and 150 wounded in a huge explosion that rocked the eastern Afghan city of Jalalabad on Wednesday, an Afghan agency said.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said the mid-morning blast occurred at a police department located in a western district of the city on the main road leading to Kabul.

AIP, based in the northwestern Pakistani city of Peshawar, said the explosion was at an arms dump where the Islamic Taleban militia was storing weapons and ammunition collected from former commanders of Afghan mujahideen guerrilla groups.
It said Jalalabad hospitals were overflowing with casualties and the city administration had asked civilians to join in rescue work at the scene of the blast.
Telephone connections between Jalalabad and Peshawar were disconnected after the explosion.
It was not immediately clear if the blast was accidental or the result of sabotage against the Taleban, who captured the city in September from a group of neutral guerrilla factions.
